You are skeptic #1. A WCAG/§4 audit of Heard's "provider-sessions" screen produced this finding. Independently verify it by READING the cited code. Try to REFUTE it — default to real=false if the code already handles it, the claim is a stylistic nit, or it's not actually reachable by a user.

FILE: /Users/taha/Claude projects/TEWW apps/Therapy (Heard)/app/(provider)/provider/sessions/page.tsx
LOCATION: Lines 48–50
RULE: 4
TITLE: Invalid nested interactive elements (Link > Button)
DETAIL: The Link element wraps a Button element. This creates nested `<a><button>` which is semantically invalid and breaks keyboard navigation and screen reader interpretation. When a user presses Enter on the link, only the link activates; the button is unreachable by tab order and may be skipped by assistive technology.
SUGGESTION: Replace the Link/Button pattern with either: (1) an `<a href>` that looks like a button (safest); or (2) make the entire Card clickable via a parent link. Example: `<Link href={...} className='...'><Card as='li'>{content}</Card></Link>` or keep the interactive element singular.

Return real=true ONLY if this is a genuine, actionable accessibility/polish gap that a fix would meaningfully improve.
